note: Provides one Webform handler plugin id 'webform_entity_handler' (label Entity) that creates/updates a content entity from a submission. No configure route, no permissions, no Drush. State lives in webform.webform.<id> under handlers.<handler_id> (id: webform_entity_handler, settings: operation/skip_if_exists/entity_type_id/entity_properties/entity_values/entity_revision/states). entity_type_id is '<type>:<bundle>' e.g. node:article; operation _default = create new, input:<key> = update by element. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real handler config on a seeded webform: introspection reads back the handler's target entity type / operation; execution adds a handler to a handler-less webform, or retargets an existing handler, verified via Webform::getHandlers() on the live site.

evals.prompt: I want a Drupal Webform to create a node every time someone submits it. Which module/handler does that and how do I attach it to a webform?
evals.expected_output: Use the Webform Entity Handler module's 'Entity' handler (plugin id webform_entity_handler). On the webform go to Settings > Emails/Handlers > Add handler > Entity, pick the entity type/bundle and operation, and map submission elements to the entity's fields.

evals.prompt: In the webform_entity_handler 'Entity' handler settings, which key stores the target entity type and bundle, and what is the format of its value? How do you tell it to create a new entity versus update an existing one?
evals.expected_output: entity_type_id holds '<entity_type>:<bundle>' (e.g. node:article). The operation setting controls create vs update: '_default' creates a new entity, while 'input:<element_key>' updates the entity whose ID is stored in that submission element.

evals.prompt: With the webform_entity_handler Entity handler, how do I map a submission element's value onto an entity field, and how do I set a field to NULL? Do tokens work?
evals.expected_output: In entity_values[field][property] use 'input:<element_key>' (pipe path 'input:parent|child' for composites) to copy a submitted value, '_null_' to set NULL, or any literal which is token-replaced. The handler has tokens=TRUE so tokens are supported everywhere.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the webform with machine name weh_known has a Webform Entity Handler attached. Inspect the live webform configuration and state which entity type and bundle that handler creates.
evals.expected_output: The handler on weh_known has settings.entity_type_id = node:article, so it creates Article nodes (operation _default = create new).

evals.prompt: The webform weh_known on this site has a Webform Entity Handler. Inspect its live configuration and say whether it is configured to create a brand-new entity or to update an existing one (name the operation value).
evals.expected_output: The handler settings.operation is '_default', which means it creates a new entity (an existing-entity update would use 'input:<element_key>' or a custom entity ID).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a webform with machine name weh_task that currently has no handlers. Using webform_entity_handler, add an 'Entity' handler to it that creates a node of type Article (node:article) on completed submissions, and save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The webform weh_task gains a handler with plugin id webform_entity_handler whose settings.entity_type_id = node:article (add it via the handler manager or the Handlers UI and save the webform).

evals.prompt: The webform weh_retarget on this site has a Webform Entity Handler that currently creates Article nodes (node:article). Change that handler so it creates Basic page nodes (node:page) instead, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On weh_retarget the webform_entity_handler handler's settings.entity_type_id is changed from node:article to node:page and the webform is saved.
